utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogunovic. A reference is also made to those men being armed. Mr. Bogunovic, is it true that at the time which is the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992, almost everybody in Ilok and the general area of Ilok was armed?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a lot of weapons. People carried weapons, people had weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bogunovic. Mr. Bogunovic, is it true that you never saw Franko Simatovic, aka Frenki, either in Ilok or in the territory of Eastern Slavonia?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never met him, never in my whole life.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Bogunovic, as it is stated in paragraph 7 of your 2007 statement that you didn't know whether there was just one commander of the Red Berets or were there several commanders of Red Berets in Ilok at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, I really knew very little about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand, you had several encounters with members of the Red Berets. Is it correct that on such occasions those people obviously didn't tell you anything about why they were there and the way their unit was structured? They also didn't mention who was in command?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't say any of that. None of us in civilian bodies knew about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, is it correct, and it is my understanding of your words so far, that you did not know who this unit belonged to in organisational terms?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, I didn't know who they belonged to and who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, in your statement which is P554, paragraph 7, that is the 2007 statement, you say that some of the Red Beret in Ilok always mentioned Franko Simatovic as their boss, and I think you also mentioned the word "commander." Is it because you were not aware of the relationship between Frenki and those men?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I truly didn't know whether he was their boss or commander. I was in no position to know and I still don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have you heard -- strike that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document 2D169. It's a 65 ter document. Your Honour, we don't have a translation of this document. By your leave, I would like to ask the witness to have a look at it and to have it MFI'd. We should make use of the presence of this witness to tell us whether he knows anything about that, and then the fate of the document should be decided upon later once we received a translation. I apologise for that, and could we please do as I propose.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, unfortunately we just got notice of this document today. So had we gotten notice about it at the beginning of examination yesterday, of course I would have sat down with the language assistant and we could go by that. I do not know what the document states.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which document are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the heading is JSO, the MUP of Krajina in Ilok, the 20th of June, 1992. It is a report which has to do with traffic control and interviews conducted. It has to do with what the witness testified about yesterday, that is why I wanted to show it to him and ask him whether the contents tally with what he could observe those people doing in the area of Ilok. We have D68 which is also from that set, it is almost identical. And I wanted to show it to the witness as well to ask him whether it reflects what he was able to observe. That's all. Perhaps to simplify matters, I can show only D68 to the witness and then we would have dealt with the problem. So let's skip the document for which we don't have a translation and we can move on directly to D68.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, I don't know if you have D68 before you.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still don't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We still do not have access to e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We can't hear Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrovic, you have not been translated because the interpreters couldn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: His microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrovic, your mike is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies. I said that it may have been marked as 2D77 and forwarded as such to the Registrar for witness's perusal. Perhaps she can use that designation. It is D68 otherwise. It is a document of the 16th of June, 1992. Please show it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, do you have it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, does what the report state reflect what you could observe those people doing, the people you referred to as the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at another document from that set. It is 2D79. May it be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrovic, before the document is taken away, where in that document can you see a reference to the Red Berets?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Anchor: How did the representatives of the Croatian Armed Forces, whose crimes you have just seen, present themselves on the eve of their surrender to the representatives of the JNA? utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, could you recognise General Biorcevic on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you recognise Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, immediately next to him?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Here we can see General Biorcevic and Arkan with Croatian prisoners. Do you recognise any of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, this was filmed immediately after the liberation of Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My question is this: At the time after the liberation of Vukovar around the 20 of November 1991, did you know that a few weeks before Arkan had killed certain people in Dalj, and you've testified about that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you think that General Biorcevic could have known that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bogunovic, did you know about very close co-operation between Biorcevic and Arkan in the territory of Eastern Slavonia and Western Srem?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If I put it to you that there was indeed very close co-operation between the representatives of the JNA and especially General Biorcevic and Arkan, would that fact explain why neither you nor any other member of the government could do anything against Zeljko Raznjatovic, Arkan, at the time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this portion of the clip be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As to the specific clip, the Prosecution does have an objection. It largely contained the narration of a reporter. The second thing is that there's only been a very small portion of this video displayed. I don't know if counsel intends to submit a greater portion into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Your Honours, with regard to the first objection by my learned friend, Mr. Weber, I agree, we will not be concerned with what the anchor said. utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Petrovic, I have a question. You have played part of that video, a portion of that clip. What you are tendering is just that portion that we saw, or are you seeking to tender the whole video?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that we should play the entire video-clip and then we would ask for the admission of the entire video-clip. utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, in this video-clip -- actually, the video material contains hours and hours, but we obviously don't want to burden the Trial Chamber with that. utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I know we are taking up time with this. That's fine, no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what will be admitted is that portion of the video you referred to, i.e., from 7.29 until 11.21. utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Petrovic, I would like to reminds you that you have little time left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... if I don't have any more time, but I would nevertheless ask for a couple of more minutes and just one second to consult with my client, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. The Simatovic Defence have no further questions for this witness. Thank you, Mr. Bogunovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. I don't know whether -- do you have many questions, Mr. Weber, to put --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bogunovic, the Chamber has a few questions to put to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must admit that I did not quite understand all the answers you gave as to the position of the Red Berets in the region where you were. We saw a number of documents where the Red Berets apparently were part of the Ministry of the Interior MUP. We have seen documents where it was said that the JNA was trying to get rid of the paramilitary forces. We have seen or you have told us that the Yugoslav Army was working in close co-operation with Arkan and the Red Berets, so finally, these Red Berets, what was their position in your region? Were they accepted or not? And how come you did not know who was in charge of the Red Berets? I'm sorry, I asked you many questions at the same time, but could you please explain what the position of the Red Berets was in Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I didn't know why they had come, who their commander or boss was. I did not have any points of reference. I was not in a position to know why they were there, whether they had come to assist in restoring peace and order, or whether they were there to do things unbeknownst to us. As far as the relationship between the Red Berets and the military authorities is concerned, they -- that was non-existent but because the military had already withdrawn from Ilok and as far as their relationship with the police is concerned, I was no longer in the police, and I didn't know that they were co-operating with the police. In any case, initially that was not the case and later on in the course of 1992, they may have been tasked with that. As I am a saying at first there was no co-operation between the police and the Red Berets, and it was only 1992 that they were given a task to control vehicles, passengers, and the rest of the things in that area of Srem and Baranja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which means that when you were minister of the interior you had no relationship whatsoever with the Red Berets or they were not yet there, or how was it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV BOGUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had not arrived yet. They were not in Ilok yet. I did not have an occasion to see them, to meet them, to be introduced to them. And my successor, I don't know whether he knew, whether he had any sources of information about them. As for me, I didn't know why they had arrived, and I could only repeat my previous answers to your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Are there any further questions you want to put to the witness? If such is the case, if there are no further questions, Mr. Bogunovic, the Chamber wishes to thank you and you can now leave. Good-bye.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And good-bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD

utterances.text: Would Your Honours like the witness to take the oath?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, could you please read the official oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a slight problem. I don't know what the problem is. Let me confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We can see it on our screens so you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Witness JF-050, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this pseudonym sheet into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, I'm going to ask you to confirm some of the previous information you've provided to the Tribunal. Did you provide two statements to the Office of the Prosecution, one of them dated the 13th to the 15th of December, 1998, and the other dated the 25th of February, 1999?

utterances.text: And did you testify in a prior case before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JF-050

utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review your prior statements and your prior testimony in your own language before you came to court today?

utterances.speaker: JF-050

utterances.speaker: JF-050

utterances.speaker: JF-050

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time the Prosecution tenders into evidence the prior statements, testimony, and proofing note for this witness. Those are 65 ter 5370, 5371, 5372, and 5378 under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's no objections so these documents are tendered under seal, and could you please give them a number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 5370 will be D80 under seal. 65 ter 5371 will be D81 under seal. 65 ter 5372 will be D82 under seal, and 65 ter 5378 will be D82 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry for the interruption, perhaps we could have Prosecution numbers instead of Defence numbers, unless that -- perhaps I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That will be P570 up it to P573 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And these documents have been admitted contrary to what I read in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. In addition, the Prosecution -- in relation to the related exhibits to the witness's prior testimony, the Prosecution submits as follows with respect to the photo albums listed in the related exhibits list as 65 ter 5373, 5374, 5375, and 5376. As was the subject of out of court informal correspondence prior to today's hearing, the Prosecution recognizes that there are some challenges posed by the use of a different numbering system developed by the investigator which was used in the statements and testimony in relation to this witness. The Prosecution prepared indexes and forwarded those to the Defence and Chambers in advance of this witness's testimony to facilitate the cross-referencing of photographs. In addition, Your Honours, the Prosecution has made selections from among these photographs, which it is seeking to tender as part of the witness's 92 ter package as related exhibits to his statement and testimony. It is in the form of a spreadsheet of photographs from these albums including those discussed by the witness with the investigator's number referenced, the ERN, the page reference to the witness's statement, and the witness's comments. In making its selection, the Prosecution sought to strike a balance between including photographs of individuals discussed by the witness in his evidence while eliminating duplications. In a very few instances where the quality of the photo or the still was extremely poor, this photo was not selected by the Prosecution for that reason. It is the Prosecution's hope that this demonstrative exhibit will facilitate the work of the Chamber and the Defence. May I request private session for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have private session for the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So to summarise, Your Honours, the Prosecution tenders eight related exhibits into evidence as they are. utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, no objections. So these documents will be admitted, some of them under seal, and I suppose the Registrar will provide us with a list with the exhibit numbers of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, I will now be reading out a public summary of your evidence. Please note that what I'm reading now is not evidence in this case. It is merely a means of informing the public of the general nature of the information you will be providing to the Court. Witness JF-050 is a Bosnian Croat who was captured by the VRS in --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: You are kindly asked to read more slowly for the interpretation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I will do so. Captured by the VRS in 1992 and detained by the VRS and other associated armed groups until June of 1995 when he was detained by Arkan and put to forced labour for his unit, the Tigers. The witness was held by Arkan and put to work as part of his work unit from June to October 1995 during the time that Arkan and his Tigers were operating in the regions of Mrkonjic Grad, Kljuc, Sanski Most, and other regions. The witness was then forced to move along with Arkan's Tigers to their training camp in Erdut in October 1995 where he stayed until March 1996. During this time, the witness was able to observe the structure of Arkan's Tigers including the distinction of regular Tigers from a group known as the Super Tigers who were said to be the original members of the unit and who were able to operate outside the rules the rest of the Tigers had to abide by. The witness saw several crimes committed by Arkan's Men such as the beating and killing of prisoners of war and on one occasion he saw Arkan himself shoot a prisoner in the chest. In early March of 1996, the witness was asked to go to a location near Erdut with several of Arkan's Men and cover over a well with soil to remove it from sight. The witness overheard one of Arkan's Men say that this well was the location of a mass grave containing victims from the Vukovar region from the years of 1991 to 1992. In March 1996, the witness was forced to move along with Arkan's Tigers to Djeletovci to the military base of the Skorpions. In approximately April of 1996, Arkan's forces and the Skorpions pulled out of this region and Arkan relocated his forces to Belgrade. The witness also states that he and the other men were ordered to loot weekend homes in Erdut upon the departure of Arkan's Unit for Belgrade. The witness was thereafter put to forced labour in Belgrade at various locations owned and run by Arkan through until July 1997. The witness will testify that the names of several of the persons whom the witness describes in his statement, some of whom were Arkan's Tigers or Super Tigers appear on the DB payment records spanning from 1993 through to the end of 1995. That concludes the public summary of the evidence of Witness JF-050.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You described in your statement and in your prior testimony being detained in a camp called Stari Mlin near Prnjavor. You say the Wolves under Veljko Milankovic were in charge of this camp. Who was it who transferred you from Manjaca to Prnjavor to the base of the Wolves of Veljko Milankovic?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: The military police of the Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Was the detention centre in Prnjavor the same place as the Wolves had their base, or was it a different location?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: It was the same location.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you were detained by the Wolves from October 1992 to March 1994 at that location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to see them in training?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you come to learn who it was who was training them?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: I don't know who was training them, but I know that Veljko Milankovic was the main person around there.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What sort of uniform did the Wolves wear?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Two piece, camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you observe any other formations coming to the Wolves camp?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: One could hear vehicles come in during evenings.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you able to identify any other armed formations who came to the camp of the Wolves?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: I only know that these were predominantly military vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did those vehicles or those driving the vehicles bear any insignias of any kind?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: I wasn't able to observe that.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: JF-050, in your statement, page 7 in English and page 9 in B/C/S, that is your 1998 statement now in evidence as P570, you described Arkan coming to you personally with a few of his military policemen and arresting you. Do you recall who came along with him?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Arkan and his military policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you describe how they were dressed and whether they had any insignias?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: On the left arm they had the patch of a tiger, and on the right arm they had the patches of the Serb Volunteer Guard. The uniforms they wore were those of the NATO Alliance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You say in your statement that Arkan seems to have presumed you were deserters and that is why you were called partisans. Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Yes. We were in the street sweeping and at that time Arkan arrived with vehicles taking away all 30 of us with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Why would it have been that he would have assumed you were deserters?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: The VRS had people who preferred to go to jail than to the front lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, you describe being held in a school at Mala Manjaca along with the Tigers. Can you tell us something about that facility? What sort of a facility was it?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: It was an elementary school at Mala Manjaca, an old building. He spent the night there and the next day he headed towards Pirici and Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: When you say "he," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JF-050
utterances.text: Arkan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Marcus, I see it is quarter to 2.00 so you could possibly ask another couple of questions if they are related to the previous questions, otherwise I think that we have to call it a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we could stop here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Before we adjourn, the exhibit which has the Exhibit D79 should have Exhibit P574 under seal. So D79 becomes P574, D79 being the pseudonym sheet. So we are going to adjourn. Witness JF-050, the hearing will resume next Monday at 2.15 p.m. in this very same courtroom, and meanwhile, you are not to discuss your evidence with anyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that we have to move into private session to escort the witness outside the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing is adjourned until Monday at 2.15 p.m. in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PICARD
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of July, 2010, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25
